extracted.intended_audience: emerging television and digital platform writers considering applying to the Sundance Episodic Story Lab
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for emerging writers preparing applications and projects for the Sundance Episodic Story Lab and what to expect during participation. Covers eligibility, application materials, storytelling standards, workshop/mentorship activities, and preparatory feedback services.

rubrics_metrics.name: Age Requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Writers must be 18 years or older.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Eligibility criterion to ensure participants are adults.

rubrics_metrics.name: Original Content
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants must submit projects derived from original material or optioned adaptations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Lab requires originality in the submitted project; derivative or unlicensed material is not acceptable unless rights are secured.

rubrics_metrics.name: Emerging Writer Status / Professional Status
rubrics_metrics.description: The Lab is for emerging writers; applicants should not have sold an episodic project yet.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Intended to support writers early in their episodic careers — prior sale of an episodic project likely disqualifies an applicant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Project Rights Secured
rubrics_metrics.description: Ensure all rights are secured, with clear ownership of the content submitted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants must confirm they have the legal right to submit the project (no unclear optioning or contested ownership).

rubrics_metrics.name: Writing Sample and Pilot Synopsis
rubrics_metrics.description: Prepare a comprehensive writing sample and a detailed synopsis of your pilot.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The writing sample should showcase your voice and the pilot synopsis should clearly outline the story, structure, and stakes of the project.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission Window and Deadlines
rubrics_metrics.description: The application period typically starts in February and ends in March.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow the published submission window closely; late or early submissions outside this period may not be considered.

rubrics_metrics.name: Logline and Concise Project Pitch
rubrics_metrics.description: Craft a striking logline and a concise project pitch.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Focus on a clear, compelling sentence(s) that communicate the project's core concept and hook; this is pivotal for initial selection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Complete Application Materials
rubrics_metrics.description: Gather all required materials and complete your application with all required documents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Double-check that every requested document is included before submission — incomplete submissions are a common pitfall.

rubrics_metrics.name: Showcase Originality in Submission
rubrics_metrics.description: Highlight what makes your story stand out; original voices are celebrated at the Lab.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasize unique perspective, unusual stakes, or original character dynamics that differentiate your project.

rubrics_metrics.name: Polished Writing Sample
rubrics_metrics.description: Ensure your writing is polished and encapsulates the essence of your narrative style.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The sample should be free of basic errors and demonstrate consistent voice, tone, and command of episodic storytelling; use external readers or professional analysis if necessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Engage With Community and Resources Pre-Application
rubrics_metrics.description: Take advantage of Q&A sessions and other available resources for firsthand advice from past participants.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use community feedback, past participant insights, and informational sessions to refine your application and avoid common mistakes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid Incomplete Submissions
rubrics_metrics.description: A common pitfall is failing to include all required materials.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Meticulously check application instructions and package all items; incomplete submissions reduce chances of selection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid Vague Story Elements
rubrics_metrics.description: Make sure each aspect of your story—plot, character, theme—is well-defined and coherent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Vagueness in plot, unclear character motivations, or an ill-defined theme will weaken an application; be concrete about stakes and arcs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do Not Ignore Feedback Opportunities
rubrics_metrics.description: Missing out on feedback can be detrimental; engage with peers and mentors to refine your submission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Actively seek critique and iterate — silence or isolation in development is flagged as an anti-pattern.

rubrics_metrics.name: Develop Narrative Skills: Episodic Structure and Character Arcs
rubrics_metrics.description: Participants refine their storytelling techniques, focusing on episodic structure and character arcs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Lab emphasizes mechanics of episode-by-episode plotting, sustaining arcs across a season, and shaping characters for serialized drama or comedy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Workshops and Structured Discussions
rubrics_metrics.description: Engage in structured workshops that sharpen storytelling techniques across plot, dialogue, and structure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Workshops provide focused craft training; expect practical exercises and critique intended to tighten script elements like pacing, beats, and dialogue clarity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Simulated Writers' Rooms
rubrics_metrics.description: Experience collaborative story development, mirroring real-world industry environments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Simulated rooms teach collaborative dynamics, note-taking, breaking episodes as a team, and receiving/implementing group notes — essential for writers entering writers' rooms.

rubrics_metrics.name: One-on-One Mentorship and Tailored Feedback
rubrics_metrics.description: Receive tailored feedback from seasoned mentors who guide you through refining your project.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Individual mentorship targets specific project weaknesses and provides personalized strategies to deepen character, clarify structure, and elevate themes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Peer Feedback and Collaborative Environment
rubrics_metrics.description: Encouragement to give and receive constructive critiques from fellow writers and individualized support from mentors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A collaborative atmosphere promotes iterative improvement through peer notes and mentor-led adjustments; participants are expected to participate in reciprocal critique.

rubrics_metrics.name: Experienced Industry Guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: Mentors include accomplished showrunners, producers, and development executives who share expertise to help writers refine scripts and storytelling approaches.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mentors provide industry-savvy advice about tone, market positioning, production considerations, and professional expectations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ongoing Mentorship and Network Access
rubrics_metrics.description: Mentorship at Sundance extends beyond the Lab with sustained mentor relationships, ongoing support, and industry introductions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mentors may offer strategic career advice and make introductions to collaborators, agents, and managers — positioning participants for future opportunities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Alumni Outcomes as Quality Signals
rubrics_metrics.description: Alumni have gone on to significant industry success (examples: Cary Fukunaga, Jill Soloway, Katori Hall, Mike White, Barry Jenkins' series).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These examples illustrate the Lab's potential impact on narrative sophistication, character depth, and capacity to develop industry-recognized work; use alumni trajectories as benchmarks for the Lab's effectiveness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Emphasis on Character Depth and Narrative Strength
rubrics_metrics.description: The Lab emphasizes character depth and narrative strength, preparing writers to address trends and fresh perspectives.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Focus on creating immersive characters and cohesive narratives that can resonate with audiences and critics; the Lab fosters innovation and thematic ambition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Greenlight Coverage: Comprehensive Screenplay Assessment
rubrics_metrics.description: Greenlight Coverage offers comprehensive screenplay assessments that help writers address dialogue, structure, and character development.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Professional analysis targets core script elements and identifies concrete improvements; recommended as complementary preparation for Lab applications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Greenlight Coverage: Objective Feedback for Preparation
rubrics_metrics.description: Use objective, professional evaluations to identify strengths and areas for improvement and prepare for applications to programs like Sundance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Third-party assessments can increase application readiness by producing actionable notes and ensuring the script meets industry expectations before submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Greenlight Coverage: Craftsmanship Refinement and Script Readiness
rubrics_metrics.description: Bolster your story’s potential with well-rounded input to sharpen narrative and character dimensions and ensure enhanced script readiness and confidence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Integrate feedback to produce a polished, submission-ready sample that instills confidence when presenting your work in the Lab and to industry mentors.
